blight.lastTime: After the famine, Anton de Bary’s work on the blight helped found plant pathology, and in 1885 Pierre-Marie-Alexis Millardet introduced Bordeaux mixture, the first widely used fungicide.

ideas.title: Fast field tests for crop disease
ideas.line: Cheap tests that spot a fungus in soil or plants early could help growers quarantine farms before a strain spreads across a region.

ideas.title: Plant pathologists and crop breeders
ideas.line: Breeders and plant disease specialists may be in demand as growers look for resistant varieties of bananas, wheat and other staples.

ideas.title: Crop genetics and seed banks
ideas.line: Understanding genetic diversity, wild relatives and seed banks explains why one-variety crops fail and how new resistant lines are found.

blight.watch: Funding for resistant varieties, new quarantine rules at ports and farms, or a pathogen reaching a major exporter would show the opening.

games.lastTime: Adi Dassler persuaded Jesse Owens to wear his handmade spikes in 1936; after Owens won four golds, the Dassler brothers’ shoes became known to athletes worldwide.

ideas.title: Tools to monitor mega-event worksites
ideas.line: Apps and audits that track wages, hours and safety for workers building stadiums could help organisers and rights groups spot abuse early.

ideas.title: Sports integrity and human rights
ideas.line: Governing bodies, sponsors and broadcasters increasingly need people who assess host bids for labour, rights and corruption risks.

ideas.title: The history of sport and power
ideas.line: Studying how rulers from Rome to Berlin used games explains what a host gains, what spectators see, and what they miss.

games.watch: Sponsors adding rights clauses, hosts publishing worker data, or bids judged on human rights would show the opening.
